chapters.title: Chapter 4: Choosing the Right ITR Form

lessons.title: ITR-1 Sahaj for Salaried Individuals: What It Covers and What It Does Not

body.text: ITR-1 arrives almost fully filled in. That is the trap. The portal pre-fills what your employer, bank and depositories have reported, not what you actually earned. Your job is not to fill the form, but to audit it.

children.text: The last lesson showed who can use ITR-1. This one opens the form. When you file ITR-1 online on the e-filing portal, it is organised into five sections that you validate one by one, followed by tax payment, verification and submission. Most of the data is pulled from your Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS. Knowing what each section holds, and where pre-filled data typically goes wrong, is most of the work.

events.title: Start the Return
events.description: Log in, go to e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then File Income Tax Return. Select Assessment Year 2026-27 and the Online mode.

events.title: Status and Form
events.description: Choose Individual as your status and select ITR-1 from the dropdown. The portal shows the documents you should keep handy.

events.title: Reason for Filing and Regime
events.description: Indicate why you are filing, for example because income exceeds the basic exemption limit. The new regime is pre-selected; opt out only if the old regime is better for you.

events.title: Validate Five Sections
events.description: Personal Information, Gross Total Income, Total Deductions, Tax Paid and Total Tax Liability. Confirm or edit the pre-filled data in each.

events.title: Pay Any Balance Tax
events.description: If tax is payable, pay it through the portal before submitting, or choose to pay later and come back.

events.title: Preview, Submit, e-Verify
events.description: Preview the full return, submit it, and e-verify within 30 days. Chapter 5 covers these steps in detail.

body.caption: What Each Section of ITR-1 Holds

cells: PAN, name, date of birth, address, contact details, residential status, regime choice, bank accounts
Contact details, filing section, regime choice, all bank accounts and the refund account
Salary breakup and exempt allowances, up to two house properties, income from other sources, Section 112A long-term gains up to ₹1.25 lakh
Form 16 data reported by employers, AIS
Salary from every employer, rent received, savings and FD interest, dividends, equity gains
Chapter VI-A deductions such as 80C, 80D, 80CCD(2), 80G, with required details
Employer's TDS return data, where declared
Every deduction you are eligible for and have proof of, including those not declared to HR
TDS on salary, TDS on other income, TCS, advance tax and self-assessment tax
That every TDS entry matches 26AS and that any tax you paid yourself appears
Tax computed on your data, rebate, cess, interest and fees, and the final amount payable or refundable
Whether the result makes sense against your own rough calculation

children.text: What Changed in ITR-1 for AY 2026-27

columns.label: New or Expanded
points: Up to two house properties allowed, instead of one
Separate field for rent that could not be realised from a tenant
Tenant's PAN or Aadhaar required where the tenant deducted TDS on rent under Section 194-IB, and tenant's TAN where TDS was under Section 194-I
Secondary mobile number, email and address can be provided
More detail on past regime opt-outs and on re-entering the new regime
Transaction reference and bank IFSC for donations under 80G and political contributions under 80GGC

columns.label: Removed or Tightened
points: The Others option for exempt salary allowances is gone; only allowances listed in the form can be claimed
Retirement benefit accounts held in foreign countries no longer need to be reported in ITR-1
A representative filing for someone else, such as a deceased person, now enters only basic details: name, contact number and email
The new regime remains the default; the opt-out question is pre-answered No

body.title: The Removed Category
body.textWithBlank: From AY 2026-27, you cannot claim a salary allowance as exempt in ITR-1 by listing it under the ___ category; only allowances specifically listed in the form are allowed.
body.explanation: The Others option for exempt allowances has been removed. In the past it was often misused to claim exemptions that did not exist, which led to mismatch notices. If an allowance is not in the list, treat it as taxable salary.

children.text: A Real ITR-1, Section by Section

Kavya, 30, is a UX designer at a food delivery company in Bengaluru, in the new regime. She lives in her own flat in Bengaluru, and rents out a second flat in Mysuru. For FY 2025-26, here is where each part of her financial year lands in ITR-1.

body.caption: Kavya's Income and Where It Goes

cells: Mysuru flat: rent ₹15,000 × 12, municipal tax ₹6,000, no loan
Long-term gain on equity mutual funds
TDS deducted by her employer on salary

body.caption: Kavya's Total Tax Liability, New Regime

cells: Add: house property ₹1,21,800, other sources ₹58,200, Section 112A gain ₹70,000
Tax on ₹16,25,000 at slab rates (excluding the ₹70,000 equity gain)
Tax on ₹70,000 Section 112A gain (within ₹1.25 lakh exemption)

body.text: Why does Kavya owe ₹29,380 when her employer deducted TDS every month? Her employer computed TDS on salary alone: ₹15,25,000 less the ₹80,000 employer NPS, which gives ₹14,45,000 and ₹1,00,620 of tax with cess. The rent and interest pushed ₹1,80,000 more into her 15% and 20% slabs, and nobody deducted tax on it. Because the shortfall is ₹10,000 or more, she was also liable to pay advance tax, so the portal will add interest for the delay.

body.title: Your Turn: Rework the Balance
body.prompt: Suppose Kavya's FD interest had been ₹93,200 instead of ₹43,200, and her bank deducted ₹9,320 of TDS on it. Everything else stays the same. Her other sources income rises by ₹50,000, all taxed in the 20% slab. What is her new balance payable before interest?
body.explanation: The extra ₹50,000 of interest adds 20% × ₹50,000 = ₹10,000 of tax, plus 4% cess of ₹400, so total tax rises to ₹1,40,400. Her TDS credit rises too: ₹1,00,620 on salary plus ₹9,320 from the bank = ₹1,09,940. Balance: ₹1,40,400 − ₹1,09,940 = ₹30,460. The bank's TDS covered only about half of the extra tax, because Kavya's marginal rate is 20% while TDS on interest is 10%. Anyone in the 20% or 30% slab should expect a balance on FD interest even when TDS is deducted.

body.title: No TDS, Still Reported
body.question: Kavya's bank deducted no TDS on her ₹43,200 FD interest, because it was below the threshold. Where does this interest appear in her ITR-1?
options: Personal Information, as part of her bank account details
Gross Total Income, under income from other sources
Tax Paid, with a TDS amount of nil
Nowhere, because no TDS was deducted
body.explanation: Interest is income whether or not TDS is deducted, and it belongs under income from other sources in the Gross Total Income section. The Tax Paid section only lists tax actually deducted or paid. Skipping untaxed interest is one of the most common ITR-1 errors, and the interest is already visible in AIS.

body.label: New for AY 2026-27
body.value: Two house properties now fit in ITR-1
body.context: A salaried person like Kavya with a self-occupied home and one let-out flat no longer needs ITR-2 just because of the second property.

children.text: Edge Cases: Can ITR-1 Handle It?

body.caption: Situations Salaried Filers Commonly Ask About

cells: Arrears of salary received this year, claiming relief under Section 89
File Form 10E on the portal before filing the return
Tenant deducted TDS on the rent you received
Enter the tenant's PAN or Aadhaar, or TAN, as the form now requires
Filing on behalf of a parent who passed away during the year
Register as a representative; the form needs only your basic details
Retirement account held abroad from a previous overseas job
Other foreign assets still rule out ITR-1
Tax on startup ESOPs deferred under the special provision for eligible startups
ITR-1 allows agricultural income only up to ₹5,000

body.title: Audit Rohit's Draft ITR-1
body.scenario: Rohit, 34, works in Noida and moved from one employer to another in November 2025. He is in the new regime and prepared his ITR-1 in 20 minutes by accepting everything pre-filled. His draft: salary shows only his current employer's figures; income from other sources shows FD interest from AIS but not ₹11,000 of savings interest, since no TDS was cut on it; the rent from his let-out flat is entered, and his tenant deducted TDS on it, but he left the tenant's PAN blank; under exempt allowances he entered ₹40,000 of 'internet reimbursement' under Others, as he did last year; and he plans to file on 10 August 2026 because he is busy in July.
body.prompt: List every problem in Rohit's draft and what he should do about each.
body.modelAnswer: First, salary is incomplete. Having switched jobs, he has two Form 16s, and the pre-fill may not reflect both correctly. He must enter salary from both employers, claim the standard deduction only once, and expect some tax to be payable, since each employer computed TDS in isolation. Second, the ₹11,000 of savings interest must be added under income from other sources. No TDS does not mean no tax, and there is no savings interest deduction in the new regime. Third, the tenant's PAN or Aadhaar is now mandatory where the tenant deducted TDS on rent, so he needs to collect it and enter it, or the TDS credit may not match. Fourth, the Others category for exempt allowances has been removed for AY 2026-27, and in the new regime most salary exemptions are not available anyway, so the ₹40,000 should be removed. Fifth, 10 August 2026 is after the 31 July due date for ITR-1. He would pay a late fee of ₹5,000, as his income exceeds ₹5 lakh, and he would lose the option to choose the old regime if it ever suited him. He should file by 31 July.

body.title: Validate Each Section Before You Submit
steps: Personal Information: check contact details, residential status, regime choice, and every bank account, with one pre-validated account for the refund
Gross Total Income: match salary against every Form 16, and use only allowances listed in the form
Gross Total Income: add all house property, savings interest, FD interest, dividends and Section 112A gains, including items with no TDS
Total Deductions: claim only deductions allowed in your regime, with policy numbers and other details ready
Tax Paid: tick off every TDS and TCS entry against Form 26AS, and add any self-assessment tax you paid
Total Tax Liability: compare the result with your own rough calculation and investigate any big gap
Pay any balance before submitting, then e-verify within 30 days

points: Online ITR-1 has five sections to validate: Personal Information, Gross Total Income, Total Deductions, Tax Paid and Total Tax Liability
Pre-filled data comes from your profile, Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS, and must be audited, not just accepted
For AY 2026-27, ITR-1 accepts up to two house properties and asks for more rent details, including tenant PAN or TAN where TDS was deducted
The Others category for exempt allowances has been removed, and foreign retirement accounts no longer need to be reported in ITR-1
Employer TDS covers salary only, so rent, interest and other income often leave a balance to pay, with interest if advance tax was due
Edge cases like Section 89 relief and representative filing fit ITR-1; a third property, startup ESOP deferral, agricultural income above ₹5,000 and lottery winnings do not

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. The portal layout, ITR-1 fields and eligibility conditions reflect the AY 2026-27 forms at the time of writing and can change with portal updates or future notifications. Always follow the current instructions on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal, or consult a qualified tax professional.
